Topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digits of π

Target audience: University students (Physics/Math enthusiasts)

Section: section_1 — The Setup: A Curious Collision

Lecture lines:
Consider two blocks on a frictionless track.
One block hits another and a wall.
We count the total collisions between objects.

Planned animations:
Display two circles of different masses on screen. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Flash the lighter circle to indicate it is incoming. [Color: #FF00FF]
Show the lighter circle colliding with the heavier stationary circle. [Color: #FF00FF]

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws

Lecture lines:
Elastic collisions conserve energy and momentum.
Velocity space forms an elliptical path.
Bounces follow this energy-conserving trajectory.

Planned animations:
Display the principle of conservation of momentum. [Color: #FFFFFF] formula: p = mv
Animate momentum vectors for both objects. [Color: #FFFF00]
Show the system state changing post-collision. [Color: #00FFFF]

Section: section_3 — The Mass Ratio Connection

Lecture lines:
Collision counts depend on mass ratios.
Mass ratios follow powers of one hundred.
Bounces reveal consecutive digits of pi.
Higher ratios yield more pi digits.
This links mechanics to number theory.

Planned animations:
Display the ratio of the two masses as M/m. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Scale the mass ratio visualization visually. [Color: #FF6600]
Highlight the relationship between mass ratio and collision count. [Color: #00FF00]

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the Unfolding π

Lecture lines:
Phase space motion describes circular arcs.
Projections extract pi digits in base ten.
Mechanics bridges geometry and number theory.
Each collision updates our digital scoreboard.
The unfolding process visualizes pi's sequence.

Planned animations:
Display the first few digits of pi on screen. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Show collision events incrementing a counter. [Color: #FFFF00] counter: 0
Animate the counter updating with each collision. [Color: #00FF00] counter: 1, 2,...
Display the evolving approximation of pi. [Color: #FF00FF] pi_approx: 3.1...
Highlight the final resulting value of pi. [Color: #FFFFFF] pi_final: 3.14...

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Elegance of Mechanics

Lecture lines:
Circular geometry governs the collision space.
Pi naturally emerges from linear impacts.
Physics reveals profound mathematical beauty.

Planned animations:
Show a summary visualization of all collisions. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Flash the final pi result alongside mass ratio. [Color: #FFFF00]
Fade out all elements gracefully. [Color: #666666]

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

To avoid render timeouts, limit the count of independent mobjects to under 10 by consolidating them into VGroups, and use 'add_updater' on persistent mobjects rather than 'always_redraw' to eliminate per-frame instantiation overhead.
Explicitly call 'self.lecture.set_opacity(0)' after 'self.setup_layout()' if the storyboard requires a sequential reveal of lecture lines to prevent them from being immediately visible.
Do not perform arithmetic on grid coordinate strings (e.g., 'C3' + RIGHT); access the coordinate from the grid dictionary first (e.g., self.grid['C3']) and then apply vector addition.

If a storyboard asset reference points to 'none.svg' or is missing, instantiate a representative Manim primitive (e.g., Square for icons, Dot for markers) with appropriate sizing rather than attempting to load a non-existent file.
